inputs.source: UTF-8 CSV bytes, optionally including a header row.

outputs.result: Parse a UTF-8 CSV byte stream into string-valued records.

header.description: Treat the first CSV row as column names.
header.help: Use true for named columns; use false with schema for headerless CSV.

delimiter.help: For CSV operators provide one character. For Galaxy tools choose a listed delimiter name.

schema.description: Comma-separated column names for headerless CSV.
schema.help: Separate field names with commas and set header to false when supplying them.

csv_parser.example_job:
# Replace the example Item paths with Items in your target catalog.
name: Parse a UTF-8 CSV byte stream into string-valued records.
steps:
- id: read_source
  operator: item_source@1.0
  inputs: {}
  params:
    uri: context:/example/source.csv
    view: bytes
- id: process
  operator: piflow_csv_parser@2.0
  inputs:
    source: read_source
  params:
    header: true
    delimiter: ','
    schema: station_id,temperature,quality
outputs:
  result: process

outputs.result: Serialize scalar input records into a CSV byte stream.

header.description: Include a header row in the output.
header.help: Use true for named columns; use false with schema for headerless CSV.

delimiter.help: For CSV operators provide one character. For Galaxy tools choose a listed delimiter name.

csv_save.example_job:
# Replace the example Item paths with Items in your target catalog.
name: Serialize scalar input records into a CSV byte stream.
steps:
- id: read_source
  operator: item_source@1.0
  inputs: {}
  params:
    uri: context:/example/source.csv
    view: records
- id: process
  operator: piflow_csv_save@2.0
  inputs:
    source: read_source
  params:
    header: true
    delimiter: ','
outputs:
  result: process

outputs.result: Keep records that satisfy the configured SQLite predicate.

condition.description: SQLite SQL predicate applied to each record batch, e.g. quality = 0.
condition.help: Use column names from the input; quote string literals and CAST string columns for numeric comparisons.

filter.example_job:
# Replace the example Item paths with Items in your target catalog.
name: Keep records that satisfy the configured SQLite predicate.
steps:
- id: read_source
  operator: item_source@1.0
  inputs: {}
  params:
    uri: context:/example/source.csv
    view: records
- id: process
  operator: piflow_filter@2.0
  inputs:
    source: read_source
  params:
    condition: quality = '0'
outputs:
  result: process

outputs.result: Run a read-only SQLite analysis query over the input relation.

viewName.description: Relation name used to expose the input to the query.
viewName.help: Use this same relation name in the FROM clause.

sql.help: Reference viewName; use SELECT and explicitly cast text columns when numeric operations are needed.
sql.example: SELECT station_id, AVG(CAST(temperature AS REAL)) AS mean_temperature FROM observations GROUP BY station_id

execute_sql_stop.example_job:
# Replace the example Item paths with Items in your target catalog.
name: Run a read-only SQLite analysis query over the input relation.
steps:
- id: read_source
  operator: item_source@1.0
  inputs: {}
  params:
    uri: context:/example/source.csv
    view: records
- id: process
  operator: piflow_execute_sql_stop@2.0
  inputs:
    source: read_source
  params:
    viewName: observations
    sql: SELECT station_id, AVG(CAST(temperature AS REAL)) AS mean_temperature FROM
      observations GROUP BY station_id
outputs:
  result: process

inputs.left: First record stream; its key fields must match the right stream for joins.
inputs.right: Second record stream, joined by key or appended after the first stream.

outputs.result: Concatenate two record streams, merging compatible fields by name.

merge.example_job:
# Replace the example Item paths with Items in your target catalog.
name: Concatenate two record streams, merging compatible fields by name.
steps:
- id: read_left
  operator: item_source@1.0
  inputs: {}
  params:
    uri: context:/example/left.csv
    view: records
- id: read_right
  operator: item_source@1.0
  inputs: {}
  params:
    uri: context:/example/right.csv
    view: records
- id: process
  operator: piflow_merge@2.0
  inputs:
    left: read_left
    right: read_right
  params: {}
outputs:
  result: process

inputs.left: First record stream; its key fields must match the right stream for joins.
inputs.right: Second record stream, joined by key or appended after the first stream.

outputs.result: Join two record streams using the specified key columns and join mode.

joinMode.description: Join semantics: inner, left, right, or full_outer.
joinMode.help: Choose inner, left, right or full_outer according to which unmatched records should be retained.

correlationColumn.help: Provide matching field names present on both inputs, separated by commas.

join.example_job:
# Replace the example Item paths with Items in your target catalog.
name: Join two record streams using the specified key columns and join mode.
steps:
- id: read_left
  operator: item_source@1.0
  inputs: {}
  params:
    uri: context:/example/left.csv
    view: records
- id: read_right
  operator: item_source@1.0
  inputs: {}
  params:
    uri: context:/example/right.csv
    view: records
- id: process
  operator: piflow_join@2.0
  inputs:
    left: read_left
    right: read_right
  params:
    joinMode: inner
    correlationColumn: station_id
outputs:
  result: process
